::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Is there a difference between the `displaymath` and `equation*` environments?](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/5788/is-there-a-difference-between-the-displaymath-and-equation-environments), asked by [Pieter](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/210/pieter) on TeX Stack Exchange (2010-11-22; [CC BY-SA 2.5](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5/)):

> The [`amsmath` documentation][q-1] says
>
> > Basic LaTeX doesn’t provide an `equation*` environment, but rather a  functionally equivalent environment named `displaymath`.
>
> Are they *really* the same or is there a catch? Maybe in interaction with some other packages?
>
>
>   [q-1]: ftp://ftp.ams.org/pub/tex/doc/amsmath/amsldoc.pdf
:::

You can find the relevant definitions in Section 55.2 of `source2e.pdf` and lines 2523–2667 of `amsmath.sty` LaTeX aliases `\begin{displaymath}` to `\[` and `\end{displaymath}` to `\]`, where `\[` and `\]` are wrappers around `$$` with some checks.  `amsmath` redefines `\[` to `\begin{equation*}` and `\]` to `\end{equation*}`, which in turn wraps around `$$` with some checks.   So they do the same thing, and as Stefan notes, once you load `amsmath`, they literally do the same thing.
